summary: MG Flasher map slots, burbles and Max Cooling from the iDrive 6 menu
author: inotbarnacle (packaged by NBTApps)
description:
A menu under My Vehicle for a car with an MG Flasher engine tune: it sends MG Flasher's Live Control commands to the engine control unit (DME) to switch map slots and burbles, and to turn Max Cooling on or off.

What it does
- Switchable maps: slots 0 to 4
- Burbles: slots 0 to 5
- Max Cooling: on or off
- Each command is sent once, and the page shows whether the DME acknowledged it. A command that is not confirmed is never sent again by itself
- Refresh current settings reads back the active settings, when the car's readback locators are on the head unit (see Good to know)

What you need
- An NBT Evo head unit with iDrive 6 (ID6), on a software version the app was built for (see Good to know)
- NBTApps agent 1.6.0 or later
- The car's diagnostic gateway. The app tries 169.254.21.3, and if nothing answers there, looks for the gateway on the car's wired network
- An engine tune flashed with MG Flasher that has the Live Control features you use

After installing
The iDrive screen restarts. Open My Vehicle and choose MG Flasher.

Good to know
- It cannot be installed together with MHD+ Suite or Bootmod3 Suite: a car has one tune or the other
- The menu sends commands to the engine control unit. Try each one first with the car parked
- Without readback locators the page can say that the DME acknowledged a command, but not which setting is active. To read them back, put the locators for your car and tune in /var/opt/hmi/data/rw/mgflasher-live-profile.txt, in the format the author's HYBRID-AND-TUNING.md describes. This package does not write or remove that file
- It talks to the primary DME only
- It needs the diagnostic gateway and does not fall back to the car's MOST bus
- The page is laid out for the screen when the package is installed. An 800×480 or 960×480 screen gets a layout of its own. A 1280×480, 1440×540 or 1920×720 screen gets the 1280×480 layout, which the head unit scales to fit. If the screen's size cannot be read, the 1280×480 layout is used
- This package does not check the head unit's software version. The author's own installer checks the head unit's iDrive framework files, and accepts those of these NBTevo versions only: K17052I, L17252I, M17345I, M17365I, N18032I, N18092I, O18184I, P18362I, Q18491I, R19101I, R19144I, S19221I, S19322I, T18501I, T21424I, T23235J, T24081I, U19384I, V20153I, W20204I, X20511I, Y21432J, Y22292I, Y23236I and Y24073J. On another version the menu may not load
- If the app was put on this car before, with the author's desktop installer or by hand, uninstall it the same way first. NBTApps refuses to install over it
- If the app does not find the car's diagnostic gateway, put its address in a gateway-ip.txt file on the head unit: /var/opt/hmi/data/ID5/gateway-ip.txt for all of the author's apps at once, or one in the app's own folder. The shared file comes first. This package writes neither
- This is a pre-release: the package has not yet been installed on a car through NBTApps

MG Flasher is by inotbarnacle, free of charge under the MIT License. NBTApps packages the author's own builds, unchanged, with the author's agreement. It comes as it is: you install it at your own risk. It is made by inotbarnacle, not by MG Flasher. Its commands follow MG Flasher's published Live Control documentation, and its menu shows the MG Flasher logo.
